observations.scope_boundary: M6.9 originally allowed changes only to isolated routed 8216 and account-router private configuration. During r18 the user explicitly interrupted and authorized a minimal standalone 8215 repair; the exception was limited to immutable startup/static-delivery successors and the stdout log boundary. The user later explicitly authorized changing 8215 to a newly device-authorized account, then explicitly authorized an 8215-only Codex Full Access override while requiring 8216 to remain unchanged. During r21 the user explicitly requested a parallel subagent repair for a stuck 8215 startup page; that subagent restarted only the standalone Web process and installed a standalone lifecycle drop-in, while the primary r21 deployment subsequently captured and preserved the fresh 8215 baseline. The standalone credential remains isolated from the router. The 8214 deployment remained out of scope.

standalone_8215_scope_override.expected_result: Restore signed-in standalone 8215 browser and model use, reduce the uncompressed startup transfer, prevent future verbose IPC/model stdout from entering the journal, activate the separately authorized standalone account without enrolling it into the router, and later give only its Codex App Server Full Access without modifying 8216.

blockers: The verified 0.2.9 router release cannot be activated from this execution environment because the previously demonstrated sudo root-GID transition failure is unchanged and /opt/codex-account-router is not writable by the codex user. A host-privileged execution of evidence/M6.9/deploy-router-r30.sh is required; no duplicate deployment attempt was made.

The second user-authorized credential is isolated to standalone 8215. Explicit authorization to enroll it into the router is still required before the real new-request A-to-B E2E, two-binding restart verification and provider-level failover proof can run.

The narrow Peer Relay grant is valid, but the current Mac relay listener is behind two NAT layers and UDP 40000 is not reachable. A user-authorized double-port-forward or an authorized directly reachable VPS relay is required for a non-DERP 8215 data path.
residual_risks: Cross-account continuity remains unverified and is not claimed.

Pre-fix codex-web-router journal records may contain upstream IPC bodies or response headers. Per-unit deletion is unavailable without vacuuming unrelated system logs; retention and access must be handled operationally.

Release r17 removes the separate startup-shim revalidation request, r18 compresses final HTML, r19 reduces the Brotli main bundle by 120417 bytes, and r20 makes the preload content-hash URL immutable, but live usable-screen observations remain variable and do not prove a stable end-to-end speedup.

Standalone 8215 journal records created before its new stdout boundary may contain upstream IPC bodies. Per-unit deletion is unavailable without vacuuming unrelated system logs; retention and access must be handled operationally.
The main bundle remains 3.174 MB over Brotli and 13.936 MB decoded; transfer, parse and renderer work remain the dominant likely optimization area without a safe upstream chunk boundary.
The App Server timing probe shows its initialization and sampled methods are not the remaining multi-second startup component, but it does not prove an exact browser critical-path breakdown.
Browser control plugin instrumentation errors were distinct from the served page and were excluded from codex-web performance evidence.
Direct Tailnet HTTP still requires a browser compatibility shim; HTTPS remains preferable.
Every authorized Tailnet principal reaching 8216 can use the configured routed accounts and workspace authority.

Standalone 8215 now deliberately runs Codex with danger-full-access and without the outer systemd filesystem/network sandbox. Any prompt injection or malicious repository content can access everything available to the unprivileged codex Unix account; root/passwordless sudo was not granted.
R21 accepts the exact HTTP/SSE path that previously returned HTTP 405, but no post-R21 real title-generation request was sent.

R22 avoids repeated fresh model-catalog waits, but the first request after router restart or TTL expiry still depends on provider latency; the five-minute cache is in-memory only and is not an availability guarantee.

R23 deterministically removes 56354 Brotli bytes and adds two pinned modulepreload hints, but the Tailnet path remains on DERP(tok) and single-run browser timing remains variable; no stable end-to-end speedup is claimed.
Because the content-hashed main URL and identity bytes are unchanged, a browser that already cached the earlier Brotli representation can retain it until normal cache eviction.
R24 manual account selection is an in-memory preference for the next new request and is lost when the router restarts.
R24 current_route is reset on router restart until the next routed request selects an account; no production model request was sent merely to repopulate it.
R29 persists only the last validated sanitized weekly observation. It remains provider-event-dependent, and a generic 429 is intentionally not treated as proof of weekly exhaustion.

R30 drops an expired weekly snapshot during restart restoration, but an observation received by an already-running process remains visible until a later observation or restart; dynamic reset-boundary expiry is not yet implemented.
R30 0.2.9 is a verified rollback-capable candidate but is not deployed because the current execution environment lacks the required host privilege; production remains on 0.2.6.
R28 caps a weekly reset delay at the existing 24-hour circuit maximum, so a farther reset receives a bounded half-open recheck rather than sleeping until the full provider reset time.

The existing local commits 3f8723f, 776f352 and 0b93593 have test evidence but their commit messages omit the test commands required by the current AGENTS.md; history was not rewritten and later commit messages include test commands.

The narrow Mac Peer Relay grant and UDP 40000 listener are configured, but the data plane has no completed handshake and still falls back to DERP. Current 8215 transfer observations are usable but may regress until the double-NAT boundary or a directly reachable VPS relay is addressed.
